item.title: A YouTuber and streamer's channel was permanently banned for a Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival gameplay video.
item.description:
A YouTuber and streamer's channel was permanently banned for a Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival gameplay video.
French content creator J0nathan said that despite covering up the nudity in the game’s opening scenes with black boxes, his channel was removed for violating YouTube’s sex and nudity policy. “Explicit content that’s meant to be sexually gratifying isn’t allowed on YouTube,” the company told the streamer in response to an appeal upholding the ban.
Hellraiser: Revival, from Space Marine 2 developer Saber Interactive, opens with a raunchy sex scene featuring a topless woman and some BDSM play. Following that, the male character runs around for a while with their wang in the wind. While the scene is explicit, it’s essential to understanding the story and acts as the catalyst for everything that follows.
J0nathan claimed that this is the scene that got his channel banned, despite the fact uncensored gameplay of the same scene remains live on other YouTube channels. While he did add the "Not Made for Kids" label to the video, he did not age gate it, assuming that censoring the explicit scenes would be enough to satisfy YouTube.
"Since the rest of the game was just a standard horror title like Resident Evil I figured it didn't really require an age restriction, and that if anything, YouTube would just apply one later on like they always do," he said.
J0nathan had 190,000 subscribers on his channel at the time of the ban, which he told IGN was "permanent."
"My channel has been completely deleted, wiping out 10 years of hard work and destroying my main source of income," he continued. "I've never had any issues with the platform before. No warnings, no strikes, nothing. And yet they just threw me away like I was nothing.”
J0nathan said he has made attempts to run through YouTube’s appeal process, but “everything seems to be handled by AI.” His first appeal was rejected within a few minutes, and support accounts on social media responded with a generic message: "We've reviewed your case and are upholding our decision.”
“How can they possibly uphold such a decision when other videos showing the exact same scene without any censorship are still available on the platform?” he commented. “It really doesn't feel like any human being is actually reviewing these cases.”
J0nathan has a side channel but is afraid of using it because YouTube prohibits banned users from operating other channels. If he attempted it, he would run the risk of losing both channels. “I'm absolutely devastated,” he told IGN. “Beyond losing my income, I'm also losing 10 years of hard work and over 3,000 videos. The emotional impact is huge. Those videos represent a big part of my life, and losing them hurts more than I can describe.
“I've tried everything. I've reached out to my contacts, asked fellow content creators for help, but none of them have managed to get in touch with anyone at YouTube who could actually review my case. The same goes for the game developers. I've sent them emails and tagged them on X, hoping they might step in and help. I'm convinced they have contacts at YouTube to help prevent unfair bans related to their game, and yet they've completely ignored me.”
Ahead of Hellraiser's release, Saber tweeted to offer guidance to content creators concerned that their videos of the game would be at best demonetized, at worst get their channel deleted. Saber recommended content creators label all streams and videos with "appropriate age restrictions, sexual theme labels, and other necessary platform tools."
"You will need to adhere to each platform's community guidelines," Saber continued. There is no 'streamer mode,' Saber also pointed out on social media ahead of launch, "so context and intent behind your content will matter."
IGN has asked Saber Interactive for comment.
Kirk McKeand is a Contributor on IGN News. Find him on Twitter @MckKirk

item.title: Agents of SHIELD star Clark Gregg, most famous for playing Agent Phil Coulson in the first Avengers movie, has teased his involvement with the just-announced Marvel TV show, Zodiac.
item.description:
Agents of SHIELD star Clark Gregg, most famous for playing Agent Phil Coulson in the first Avengers movie, has teased his involvement with the just-announced Marvel TV show, Zodiac.
Marvel announced Zodiac at a New York Comic Con panel yesterday with a logo, below, a 2028 release window, and little else. We know it's a spy thriller and, based on the logo, it has something to do with SHIELD. Hot on the heels of the reveal, Gregg shared the announcement to his Instagram, sparking speculation that the two shows are linked.
The logo for the show features the show’s title, Zodiac, with a stylized “o” and a stylized “a.” The “a” has a little eagle head in the middle, mirroring the SHIELD logo.
"For anyone who knows the comics, if you look closely at this title design, you’ll see a few clues about where we’re going," Marvel TV head Brad Winderbaum told the audience during the announcement. "I can’t tell you anything else about it yet because it’s a secret. We're going to start casting it in a couple weeks.”
Agents of SHIELD ended back in 2020 and saw Gregg’s Agent Coulson return from beyond the grave in android form. However, the series is not listed on the Disney+ "MCU Complete Timeline" section, which features every single canon MCU movie, TV series, and one-off special, so its place in official Marvel canon is unclear.
Chloe Bennet, who played Daisy, recently said she's "still low-key angry" that Agents of SHIELD isn't considered fully part of MCU canon — though has insisted she would reprise her role if asked. Fans are hoping to see the return of Samuel L. Jackson’s Nick Fury in Zodiac, which is named after a criminal organization made up of bad guys named after zodiac signs. Nick Fury’s brother, Scorpio, is one of them.
Of course, there’s been no official word on where Zodiac will go. All we know is that it’s a spy thriller, and if it goes in another direction to the comics, it wouldn’t be the first time for the MCU.
Elsewhere in Marvel TV shows, Daredevil: Born Again will end with Season 3. Ahead of that wrapping up, VisionQuest is landing on Disney+ on October 14, and the showrunners said they didn’t pay much attention to the wider MCU when putting the story together.
VisionQuest sees Paul Bettany reprise his role as Vision on the run from people seeking to weaponize him. The limited series will be eight episodes long. In case you missed it, here's everything announced at the Marvel TV and Animation panel at NYCC 2026.
Photo by Mitch Haaseth via Getty Images.

item.title: Earlier this week, Marvel announced that it was discontinuing the Marvel Unlimited app, only to have it replaced by the new Marvel Comics app, powered by Webtoon. At New York Comic Con I had the chance to go hands-on with the app, and I am struggling to see why it needs to exist.
item.description:
Earlier this week, Marvel announced that it was discontinuing the Marvel Unlimited app, only to have it replaced by the new Marvel Comics app, powered by Webtoon. At New York Comic Con, I had the chance to go hands-on with the app, and I am struggling to see why it needs to exist.
Just like Marvel Unlimited, the new Marvel Comics app will bring the entire Marvel and Star Wars comics libraries at both of its subscription tiers. On the surface, the big advantage Webtoon has over Unlimited is how quickly new comics will be available — with the more expensive ‘Ultimate’ tier getting new issues 30 days after print, rather than Unlimited’s 90-day waiting period.
Webtoon shared a rough roadmap for the app; it’s looking to bring in Disney and Pixar comics, make it easier to create your own custom lists, and create different profiles for all the comics readers in your home – even kids. But, Webtoon failed to share dates for when any of these improvements are coming, so at least for now, it looks like the bulk of the changes are minor cosmetic ones.
Webtoon said that its mission in designing this app was to make it faster and easier to use. After all, Unlimited has been around since 2007, and the UI still kind of looks like it’s stuck about a decade in the past. But rather than give Marvel Unlimited a facelift, the decision was made to create a brand new app. While the navigation does seem a bit more modernized, the app itself isn’t noticeably faster than Unlimited was. Of course, this could come down to the tablets at the Webtoon booth and spotty convention Wi-Fi, but I couldn’t really feel the difference.
Once you click into an issue, the Marvel Comics app does get a bit more compelling. Before you start reading the issue, it’ll bring you into a sort of overview page, where you’ll be able to see the information about the selected issue, but you’ll also be able to slide through other issues in the series on the top of the screen. There’s also a section where you’ll be able to see every reading guide that issue is a part of.
When I’m reading comics on the Unlimited app, I tend to make a beeline straight for reading guides, because I simply don’t have the patience to read entire comics runs that sometimes have hundreds of issues. Marvel Unlimited’s reading guides were excellent, and it seems like they’ve carried over to the Webtoon app. But, again, I only had a few minutes with the app in a crowded booth at NYCC, so I didn’t exactly have time to see if all of my favorite guides were intact.
Once you get into an actual comic, though, not much has changed. You can still choose between reading the entire page or reading panel by panel. With the latter option, you can also choose to have it zoom back out when you’re ready to move on to the next page, in order to appreciate all the art on the page, just the way you would in a regular comic.
That’s a great way to read digital comics, but Marvel Unlimited had the exact same options, and it wasn’t hard to set up. As nice as the new UI is, that probably could have been implemented with a hefty update, rather than asking all of the Marvel Unlimited users to switch over to a whole new app. The Marvel Comics app will let you move over your library and all of your reading progress, but I can only imagine that there are going to be people who stubbornly won’t make the migration. I just hope it was worth that risk.
The new Marvel Comics app launches November 16 with more than 35,000 digital comics. Marvel Unlimited will sunset on December 7, 2026.
Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

item.title: As reported by Denfaminicogamer, Nier creator Yoko Taro was asked if he had any current projects or plans to make a new game. He replied, “nothing really,” and confessed that “I’m done with working. I don’t want to do it anymore.”
item.description:
NieR franchise creator Yoko Taro dropped a big revelation about his motivations for continuing to work and his thoughts on the future of Japan’s game industry. As reported by Denfaminicogamer, Taro was asked if he had any current projects or plans to make a new game. He replied “nothing really,” and confessed that “I’m done with working. I don’t want to do it anymore.”
On top of this, Taro revealed that he already achieved his life goal before he even made critically-acclaimed titles like NieR Automata. Taro's first game as director was 2003 PS2 title Drakengard (known as Drag-on Dragoon in Japan). “With Drakengard, the first game I was given the opportunity to direct, I was actually able to do almost everything the way I wanted,” he said, noting that he was able to release a game that “represented the best I could do at the time.”
“As a game otaku, I think the dream is to release something you’ve always wanted to create into the world. Having achieved that dream, I view everything after that as the remainder of my life,” he continued. Taro went on to reveal that he merely continued working because he’d be in trouble if he had no income.
Recently, he has considered retiring as he believes his savings and pension would be enough. However, he has a fear of developing dementia in old age, noting that he has heard of people being diagnosed with the disorder after retiring, and it is this fear that motivates him to keep working. So when he faces a difficult situation at work, he gets through it by telling himself: “This is good for preventing dementia.”
Taro made these revelations during a talk session with Ender Lilies and Ender Magnolia director Keisuke Okabe at The Tenth Mosaic video game culture festival held at the Tokyo French Institute last month. Of course, Taro is well-known for making eccentric and sometimes deadpan statements from under his ubiquitous Emil mask, so what he said should perhaps be taken with a grain of salt.
Regarding the future of the Japanese games industry, Taro quipped: “I’m going to die soon, so I really don’t care what happens to Japan’s game industry. However, I think that recently AI and various technologies have created a breeding ground where creators in their teens and 20s, who are even younger than Mr. Okabe, can freely create things.”
“I’m 56 now, but when people my age were young, we only had two options if we wanted to make a game: either ‘join a game company’ or ‘make a niche game for PC.’ If you wanted to make a 3D game you had no choice but to join a game company.” Taro said that the options for people who want to make games have broadened considerably since then, but this is inevitably leading to tougher competition.
“I think this competition will gradually spread like fire from the younger generations to the older generations of developers,” he commented. “As I’m already on the older side, I’m simply filled with fear and trepidation, hoping that these flames don’t reach me before I die.”
Regarding other titles and what motivates him to create games, Taro said “I don’t really get jealous of other games. When I come across something good, I end up viewing it from a fan’s perspective. This triggers my collector trait, and I just want to buy them all.”
“I’ve always worked in the games industry with the mindset of ‘filling in the gaps,’ he explained. “For example, I really like games like ICO and (Treasure’s bullet hell shooter) Ikaruga, but when I played them they were so perfect that I thought, ‘I don’t need to make games in these genres.’ That’s not jealousy, it’s the feeling of, ‘This gap has already been filled, so I need to fill a different one.’ I think the reason that my games are crude games full of terrible things is because the pioneers have already seized all the beautiful aspects.”
Since 2021’s Nier Reincarnation and the reboot of Nier Replicant, Taro has worked on the Voice of Cards RPG series and 2024 mobile title 404 GAME RE:SET. He is currently writing the upcoming as-yet untitled Neon Genesis Evangelion TV series, with NieR and Drakengard composer Keiichi Okabe providing the music.
Of course, Nier fans are desperate for a proper follow-up, but so far nothing has been announced. In November last year, the developer said he’d been working on various projects, but they just keep getting canceled.
“I often get told stuff like, ‘Why aren’t you making a new sequel to NieR?’ or, ‘Yoko Taro isn’t doing anything,’ but that’s because recently, a lot of projects I was involved in got discontinued midway through development," he said.
"I’ve actually been working on some stuff, it’s just that it never ended up seeing the light of day. I got paid for it, so I personally have no issues with that, but people seem to think that I haven’t been doing anything just because none of the work I’ve done is being released."
Verity Townsend is a Japan-based freelance writer who previously served as editor, contributor and translator for the game news site Automaton West. She has also written about Japanese culture and movies for various publications.

item.title: At New York Comic Con, VisionQuest showrunner Terry Matalas told IGN's Jeffrey Vega that MCU boss Kevin Feige gave Matalas a pass on doing whatever he wanted, as long as he included one particular thing.
item.description:
Marvel's upcoming TV show VisionQuest took one last lap at New York Comic Con 2026 ahead of its release on Disney+ on October 14. As part of Marvel's Television and Animation panel, the cast — Paul Bettany, James Spader, Emily Hampshire, and Ruaridh Mollica — and showrunner Terry Matalas came on stage to greet the crowd before screening the series' first episode for the room.
After the panel, IGN's Jeffrey Vega asked Matalas about the writing process for VisionQuest. How much did the writers have to weave around the bigger picture of the MCU? Turns out, not too much.
"There was a couple of early ideas that we would talk about with Kevin [Feige] and be like, 'Well, what about this?'" Matalas said. "And you could quickly read his temperature. But we pretty much did exactly what we [wanted] with these — I had a brilliant writing staff that we conceived in the room and I think it's all on the screen."
The cast and creator of Marvel Television’s #VisionQuest take the #NYCC stage! https://t.co/AmpRbr67ZT
Matalas said he was given a a lot of freedom to explore what happened to Vision after White Vision flies off at the end of WandaVision, and approached thinking about the many possibilities of a blank slate "organically."
"Time has passed for the audience and I think you want to lean into that. What has [Vision] been up to? Where has he been? I think him being on this identity quest, trying to figure out, 'Am I the old Vision? Am I something new? What am I?' It sort of all came together pretty quick," Matalas said. "The only thing I knew for sure from Kevin [Feige] when he called about it was he's going to reunite with his son. He's like, 'The rest is up to you.' And I was like, 'Okay.' I remember very clearly I was at home. I hung up the phone and I was like, 'Well, who's [Vision] talking to? Because Tommy feels like a thing he's got to get to.' And I was like, 'It's Ultron. It's Ultron.' And then I was like, 'How do I get to Ultron?' Ultron was dead."
The first VisionQuest reactions are out from its debut screening at NYCC and they're positive, calling it a "worthy successor to WandaVision." Now, let's see if Wanda shows up when VisionQuest premieres.
Leanne Butkovic (she/they) is an Editorial Programming Manager at IGN, where they've also written about TV, movies, and games.

item.title: Finn Jones addresses his return as Danny Rand/Iron Fist in Daredevil: Born Again Season 3, calling a second chance with Marvel a 'wonderful gift.'
item.description:
Speaking with IGN at New York Comic Con 2026, Iron Fist actor Finn Jones calls his return to the MCU as Danny Rand in Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 “a wonderful gift” and shed light on how his character has “evolved” since The Defenders.
“It's wild to not play a character for 10 years and then come back after all that time. For an actor, it's a wonderful gift,” Jones told us following the Marvel Television panel. “I think personally people grow a lot in 10 years and as an actor you grow a lot, and characters grow a lot as well. So to come back with all of that kind of story and to bring that forward into this what I see is it's kind of like a new version of Danny Rand or a more of an evolved, grownup version is really fun. So fun.”
While Jones couldn’t reveal too much about what happens with Danny in the upcoming third and final season of Daredevil: Born Again, he told us how he imagined his own backstory of what the character has been up to in the many years since he was last seen.
“I think he's been around the world in various different secret orders, probably a lot of like down in ancient ruins in South America and in Asia and really honing his craft,” says Jones. “I think he's gone through a lot of grief and a lot of joy and I think that's really forged the Danny that we see show up in Daredevil Season 3. That's all my own backstory. That's just like where I believe the character has been and then what we see in the show is I think a culmination of that.”
Jones calls the Danny Rand in Daredevil: Born Again “very, very grounded” and with “a different quality to him, which is just a joy to play.”
Jones also recalled what it was like to step back on set opposite his fellow Defenders co-stars Charlie Cox (Daredevil), Krysten Ritter (Jessica Jones) and Mike Colter (Luke Cage).
“It was so charged, you know, like a lot of anticipation and so there was definitely nerves, but there was also a lot of excitement. And I think when you're in that kind of environment, it allows you to really sharpen and focus [on] what you want to bring. And so, it just felt very dynamic,” says Jones. “Being with these guys again – with Charlie and Krysten and Mike – there's such a great chemistry between all four of us that you can really just relax into the dynamic that's just between us all.”
“The way that they've written Danny this year is – I'm just so grateful. I'm just so grateful [for] the level of attention that's been put into the character. And I remember getting the scripts and I was just like, ‘I got no notes.’ I'm just ready to show up and give my all.
Jones adds, “And I have to say the stunt team working with [coordinator] Phil Silvera and his team have been really they're they're the best. They are the best and I'm so grateful to have them be so supportive and so imaginative bringing Danny Rand back into the MCU.”
Daredevil: Born Again returns for its final season in 2027.
Jim Vejvoda (he/him) is IGN's Assoc. Director of Entertainment Content.

item.title: Daredevil star Charlie Cox has confirmed that he is starring in another video game, this one for Sega.
item.description:
Daredevil star Charlie Cox has confirmed that he is starring in another video game, this one for Sega.
Cox opened up about the project at New York Comic-Con 2026, telling IGN’s Jeffrey Vega that he’s completed recording for an as-yet unannounced Sega video game.
“I did another one! It doesn’t have a name yet,” he said. “I did a Sega one. I’ve done one since. It hasn’t come out yet. It was fun to do. It’s hard. It’s a whole different job, man.”
Cox went on to share a humorous anecdote about his experience working on the game, saying that the crew weren’t aware that he wasn’t American.
“I’m not sure what I’m allowed to say, but I showed up for it, and I met them for the first time, they asked me to do this game, and so I agreed to it. Then I had to do 40 hours or whatever it was, and I showed up for the first day, and I was like, ‘Hi guys, nice to meet you! How are you?’ And all of them went, ‘...oh, he’s English.’ They’d hoped, they’d wanted him to be American. But now I’ve got to do 40 hours of lines I’ve not prepared in an accent. Yeah, I think they thought I was American.”
This, at least, gives us one bit of information about his role in the mysterious game — he’ll be playing an American character (or at least, a character with an American accent), and it’s likely that his role will be central to the plot, given that he recorded 40 hours’ worth of lines for it.
It's also worth noting that Cox confirmed he was working on a new game earlier this year, though he similarly declined to mention many details at the time.
Thus far, that’s all we know. Cox has already proven his voice acting chops with Expedition 33, where he played Gustave, famously recording all of his lines in a mere four-hour session. Players lauded his performance after the game released in 2025, and he was even nominated for Best Performance at the Game Awards that year.
Sega’s upcoming lineup of video game releases includes Stranger Than Heaven, Virtua Fighter Crossroads, Persona 6, and Alien: Isolation 2, among several others. Given that this particular project doesn’t even have a name yet, it’s unlikely that it’s any of these that have already been announced, so we’ll just have to wait and see what’s in store.
In the meantime, fans of Charlie Cox can look forward to Daredevil: Born Again Season 3, though this is set to be the end of Matt Murdock’s current adventures — at least for the time being. The news broke in late September alongside reports that its showrunner, Dario Scardapane, exited the series while it was in post-production.
Kingpin actor Vincent D’Onofrio penned a heartfelt goodbye to the series on social media, writing, “We have the final Season, season 3 heading your way next year with some very cool stuff. Much love to all who have been supportive. I love that character Fisk. Always will. Off to another neck off the woods. Meanwhile… Season 3 is coming!”
Daredevil Born Again: Season 3 is set to release in early 2027.

item.title: Charlie Cox is telling fans to "get the Save Daredevil Campaign" going as Daredevil: Born Again Season 3 will be the show's last.
item.description:
Charlie Cox hit New York Comic Con today to join in the Marvel Television panel — jetlagged and just in from Dublin, but ready to talk the return of Daredevil for Season 3 of Born Again. And not just the return of the Horned One, but also his old teammates The Defenders.
"I think there needed to be a full circle with that story," Cox told IGN's Jeffrey Vega today after the panel. "There needed to be some kind of closure with it."
The Defenders of course originated in the Netflix Marvel era, where each character — Daredevil, Jessica Jones (Krysten Ritter), Luke Cage (Mike Colter), and Iron Fist (Finn Jones) — had their own series before teaming up for the 2017 Defenders season. Eventually those shows all came to an end, but when Cox and Vincent D'Onofrio showed up in the proper MCU, it seemed like only a matter of time before the street-level heroes would be reunited.
Charlie Cox, Finn Jones, and Krysten Ritter reunite on the #NYCC stage! #Daredevil https://t.co/XUJ200rP8w
"And Marvel were willing and able to bring them back and have a lot of fun with it," the actor said of the quartet returning. "It was great. We're such good friends. We have a great time together. There's some really interesting, fun dynamics that the fans seem to love, so it was great."
Part of that fun, Cox joked, was Mike Colter "giving away spoilers non-stop" — referring of course to the actor putting some info on social earlier this year that he shouldn't have. "We had to ban him from getting sides on set!"
As for whether or not Born Again Season 3, which has been confirmed to be the last season of the show, means we won't see Cox put on the horns again, the actor says it might be up to the fans to decide on that front.
"Don't know, man. I don't know," he said when asked whether or not he's done as Daredevil. "I mean, it might be. It might be. Don't worry about Kevin [Feige]. Get the Save Daredevil campaign on the horn. Get them motivated. That engine, that won't stop until there's some resolution. That's my true superpower -- is the Save Daredevil campaign!"
Talk to Scott Collura @scottcollura.bsky.social, or listen to his Star Trek podcast, Transporter Room 3. Or do both!
Jeffrey Vega is the Lead Social Host/Producer at IGN and is probably feeding his neopets right now. You can follow him on Twitter @jeffreyvega, Instagram, and IGN's TikTok.

item.title: Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture turns Kevin Smith’s View Askewniverse into a foul-mouthed cozy weed farming simulator. New details and the first trailer were revealed at New York Comic Con 2026.
item.description:
Nitrate Games revealed the first footage and new details about its upcoming farm sim video game Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture at New York Comic Con on Thursday. IGN can exclusively share the first trailer for the game, which you can watch via the player embedded below.
Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture promises a funny and raunchy spin on the cozy farming genre, with creator Kevin Smith’s iconic characters out to “build the best weed farm in town.” Players will build, cultivate and expand their operation, interact with familiar faces, and experience an original story written by Ernie Altbacker (the animated films Batman: Hush and Justice League Dark).
Kevin Smith and Jason Mewes have been creative forces on the project from the start.
“Since Jay and Silent Bob are the stars of this hilarious growing game, I cannot wait to play with myself!,” said Kevin Smith in a statement provided to IGN. “Many thanks to Nitrate Games for taking my little animals to this crossing and making them Stars Dew a Valley!”
“Joint Venture is a Jay and Silent Bob game, but it’s actually a continuation of Kevin Smith’s View Askewniverse,” says Nitrate Games co-founder Montana Sommese. “The central narrative picks up where the films left off, making the game a kind of sequel. Players can befriend and engage with their favorite characters from Kevin Smith's movies like never before. As we update the game over time, we're excited to be able to expand Kevin's story universe with narrative updates that will continue building from his cinematic universe.”
The NYCC panel revealed that other familiar faces from the View Askewniverse appear in the game, including Clerks’ Dante, Randal and Veronica; Mallrats’ Brodie and T.S. Quint; Chasing Amy’s Holden, Banky, Hooper and Alyssa; Dogma’s Azrael and Serendipity; Clerks II’s Becky & Elias; and Mooby.
Jay and Silent Bob’s Joint Venture is currently heading toward its play testing phase of production, with an expected release in late Spring 2027 on Steam/PC. A console release is also slated for 2027. Fans can learn more and sign up to playtest and wishlist.

item.title: Smile 2 star Kyle Gallner is making it known that he’s ready and willing to play V in Paramount’s film adaptation of Cyberpunk 2077.
item.description:
Smile 2 star Kyle Gallner is making it known that he’s ready and willing to play V in Paramount’s live-action film adaptation of Cyberpunk 2077.
Cyberpunk 2077 has come a long way from its roots as a tabletop RPG. Thanks to CD Projekt Red’s video game and its standout expansion, as well as the critically-acclaimed Edgerunners spinoff anime from Studio Trigger, fans of the gritty sci-fi series are eating well.
They’re about to get fed even more, as Paramount revealed that it is developing a live-action movie based on the franchise. Thus far, we’re not sure of any plot details, so it’s possible that we could follow V’s adventures with Johnny Silverhand, or Idris Elba’s Solomon Reed before he meets V — or heck, maybe even Edgerunner 2’s Weak Kingsley, for all we know!
What we do know is that there’s no shortage of possibilities for this film, and that’s what has fans so excited. One of these fans is none other than actor Kyle Gallner, who is raring to step into Night City as the male version of V.
Mere hours after Paramount announced the news on October 8, Gallner posted a photo of himself sporting a close-shaved crop of hair, similar to V’s hairstyle in the game’s marketing materials, along with the caption: “Take me to night city.”
It’s safe to say that fans are pretty enthusiastic about this possible casting, with many already envisioning Gallner alongside Keanu Reeves’ Johnny Silverhand.
Take me to night city. https://t.co/qchq61ZW9P
“Kyle and Keanu. Sounds outstanding,” one wrote, while another said Gallner would be “PERFECT casting.”
“You and Keanu teaming up? I could be on board for that,” another commented.
“He’s HIM! Paramount, please consider,” yet another vouched.
For now, details about the movie are being kept under wraps, but CDPR co-CEO Michał Nowakowski promised that more information will come soon.
"We're excited about Paramount as a future partner who shares our creative ambitions for the Cyberpunk franchise," he said on X. "We look forward to sharing more details at the appropriate time."
While they wait for more news, fans can look forward to Edgerunners 2, set to air on Netflix on October 20, 2026.

item.title: The Dungeon Crawler Carl series has absolutely blown up this year. Matt Dinniman's LitRPG story has created some truly dedicated fans who are showing up in droves to support DCC as it transitions to a major franchise.
item.description:
The Dungeon Crawler Carl series has absolutely blown up this year. Matt Dinniman's LitRPG story has created some truly dedicated fans who are showing up in droves to support DCC as it transitions to a major franchise.
IGN's Blythe Dujardin is on the ground at NYCC this week and can confirm that Dungeon Crawler Carl is there in force this year. Most notably, all of the new action figures and toys were on full display at the show. We even got a closer look at three of the Princess Donut plushies that come in the upcoming blind box.
The Princess Posse Plush Blind Boxes were first announced back at the end of August, but we haven't gotten much more information about them since then. You can currently preorder these blind boxes directly from EBGames Canada for $19.99 with an October 30 release date.
According to information from the product page, each blind box includes one Princess Donut plush with a total of six different variations available. There doesn't seem to be a U.S.-based listing available yet, so it's unclear when you can expect them to drop in the states.
With the sudden rise in popularity, the merch side of the franchise is still trying to catch up. Playmates announced a new line of DCC action figures back in February, for example, but they are still rolling those out to major retailers this month.
The very popular Dungeon Crawler Carl tabletop games are still a couple months away, as well. The incredibly successful crowdfunding campaign wrapped up in May with just over $13 million raised for the project, which has likely sped up production, but we're still looking at a December release date for the commercial product.
With the Dungeon Crawler Carl TV series in the works at Peacock and two more books still on the way, this is likely only the first wave of DCC merch we'll see over the years. If you haven't already read the books, you can check out our guide to the series for more information.

item.title: Street Fighter 6 producer Shuhei Matsumoto revealed how dire things were for Capcom’s flagship fighting game franchise during the Street Fighter V era and explained how he and director Takayuki Nakayama worked together to save the series from death.
item.description:
Street Fighter 6 producer Shuhei Matsumoto revealed how dire things were for Capcom’s flagship fighting game franchise during the Street Fighter V era and explained how he and director Takayuki Nakayama worked together to save the series from death.
It’s no secret that Street Fighter V stumbled massively when it launched in February 2016. Many players felt that it was shipped out in an unfinished state, as it lacked basic elements like an arcade mode or story mode, on top of its incredibly unstable netplay.
Shuhei Matsumoto — who stepped in as producer for Street Fighter V near the end of its lifetime following Yoshinori Ono’s exit from Capcom in 2020 — alongside director Takayuki Nakayama, recognized that the franchise as a whole was in peril, and believed that the Street Fighter IP might actually fade into obscurity within the next decade if they didn’t act fast.
"When the two of us were talking during Street Fighter V, we realized that if we didn't do something about Street Fighter, the Street Fighter IP would probably die in 10 years. It was critical. So, we had to make it a game where people would get to know it all over again and play it again,” Matsumoto said during an October 2026 interview with Karin Ohira.
Matsumoto explained that SFV’s aging playerbase was one example of this issue, saying Capcom needed to target younger players if it wanted Street Fighter to live.
"At that time, the player base for Street Fighter V was roughly 35 to 45 years old. In 10 years, these people will be 60. It’s difficult to sustain the franchise if we only rely on that group,” he continued.
"...It had become a distant presence. People knew of the scene, but weren't actually playing the game, which made us think, 'This is bad.' In the end, we're a game company, yet people weren't playing our game. Isn't that the most fatal thing? So that was the biggest danger. We didn't know if those people would continue with the same level of passion, and naturally, there's a lifespan to things, right? That's when we talked about how, if we left it as it was, the IP would likely die in 10 years."
So, how did they manage to turn things around so dramatically with Street Fighter 6? Matsumoto said that the team avoided relying on its power as a historic IP, and decided to start with a blank slate, as if no one in the current generation knew about it, at all.
"While people say Street Fighter has high name recognition, we shouldn't be overconfident. We decided to act as if the current generation doesn't know us. We have to properly explain things to those who are just starting to play games now — like who these characters are and how to play — so we don't take that familiarity for granted."
Matsumoto also said that the development of SF6's Modern control scheme was integral to reaching a new audience, alongside other approachable features like World Tour Mode (which has since been paused for the forseeable future), the Battle Hub, and real-time commentary from community figures like Vicious and Tasty Steve.
Matsumoto and Nakayama’s plan paid off big time; Street Fighter 6 is one of Capcom’s most successful Street Fighter games of all time, having sold more than seven million lifetime units as of summer 2026. It’s extremely popular both in Japan and abroad, and boasts a massive playerbase across both Steam and consoles.
It’s a big year for Street Fighter fans and Capcom in general; the developer has released three critically-acclaimed titles in Resident Evil Requiem, Pragmata, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, and is gearing up for the Street Fighter movie on October 16, which comes on the heels of the Resident Evil adaptation directed by horror savant Zach Cregger.

item.title: Ben Affleck has revealed he plays shooters like Fortnite and sometimes ends up getting into arguments with kids in voice chat.
item.description:
Ben Affleck has revealed he plays shooters like Fortnite and sometimes ends up getting into arguments with kids in voice chat.
When speaking on the New Heights podcast, Affleck was asked about the inspiration for some of the costumes in his latest film, Animals. The new Netflix thriller features a character wearing a fuzzy bunny mask, and Affleck stated that he took inspiration from Fortnite for that particular costume. He noted that his son was taking an interest in Fortnite skins and kept calling them "tough." Affleck joked that he didn't quite understand what was "tough" about a character wearing a bunny mask, but utilized it as an inspiration.
"I thought these costumes are so kind of random and unusual, that's what I based the costumes on," said Affleck. "I thought he'd be getting them off games."
The actor also noted that he plays quite a few games himself, including sports titles like Madden and 2K, as well as shooters. Affleck joked that because of his gaming experience, he believes he's good at shooters, but realizes he's not as capable as younger players.
"I always play games," he said. "I play first person shooter games, so I think I'm good, and then 12-year-olds just f**k you up. I try to come out and I'm like, ‘Here I come.’ I get killed right away, and then they taunt you, like, ‘You suck. F**k you!’ I end up getting in arguments. ‘F**k you! I don't suck! I'm a grown man!’”
Affleck has been vocal about his love for gaming before, particularly Valorant. The actor has attended multiple Valorant events with his son, noting in the past that he mains KAY/0 in the game. He also joined the Valorant e-Sports team Sentinels for a watch party last year, where he talked about his experience with the game on stream.

item.title: We've already known that X-Men '97 Season 3 was happening, but at New York Comic Con 2026, Marvel showed the first teaser for the new season, with surprise appearances from Deadpool and She-Hulk.
item.description:
We've already known that X-Men '97 Season 3 was happening, but at New York Comic Con 2026, Marvel showed the first teaser for the new season, with surprise appearances from Deadpool and She-Hulk.
After the chaotic ending of Season 2, the X-Men are scattered, and according to Variety, the trailer shows Deadpool and She-Hulk in attendance of Rogue and Gambit's wedding – which is also a thing, apparently.
From this brief appearnace, it's not clear how big of a role either of these characters will play. It's possible that they're just in a brief cameo for the wedding. However, Deadpool is no stranger to working with the X-Men when it suits him, so we could totally see him having a bigger part.
We don't know much else about what X-Men '97 season 3 is going to be about yet, though. Back at SDCC, Marvel revealed some clips of the Brotherhood of Mutants, with Pyro, Avalanche, Toad, and Blob writing "mutant freedom" on the side of a building. Then, of course, they're attacked by a sentinel dressed in red, white, and blue paint.
But while we knew that the Brotherhood of Mutants is back, we also know who is leading them after Magneto's death at the hands of Apocalypse in season 2. The trailer shows Mystique leading the team, which opens up a ton of possibilities.
Luckily, during the SDCC panel, Executive Producer Brad Winderbaum suggested that the studio was wrapping up animation on season 3 while season 2 was finishing. Hopefully that, combined with this new trailer, means that season 3 will come out sometime next year. But we'll just have to wait for Marvel to reveal more information.

item.title: Resident Evil Requiem producer Masachika Kawata revealed that the game was originally planned to be an online title before they scrapped the idea to focus on horror.
item.description:
Resident Evil Requiem producer Masachika Kawata revealed that the game was originally planned to be an online title before they scrapped the idea to focus on horror.
Kawata shared this information in the Biohazard 30th Special Mook (‘magazine book’), a 124-page, full-color fan book with a complete history of the series' timeline, creature genealogy, and developer interviews.
“Every game is a continuous process of trial and error. For example, with Resident Evil Requiem, [game director Koshi Nakanishi] initially went so far as to develop it as an online game,” he said, via a fan translation.
“However, the results of research conducted partway through development were not favorable, so we decided to prioritize the horror concept once again and abandoned the online direction.”
That’s not the only wild thing Kawata revealed in the mook; he also said that Leon was the first character the team chose as a protagonist, but they ultimately felt that being able to hack and slash zombies with ease would lean too heavily on the "action" side of things, making the overall game less scary.
“Leon was also the first character confirmed to appear as a protagonist. However, we determined that with Leon alone, who excels in combat, ‘horror would no longer work,’ so it was decided to introduce Grace as a new character,” he continued.
Kawata also explained why Capcom decided to wait before sharing Leon’s involvement in the game, saying, “By keeping the full picture of the game, which would develop along both the horror and action sides, until the very end, we were able to successfully maintain interest in it up until release.”
Nakanishi’s early plans to make RE9 an online game isn’t something totally surprising, given that management at Capcom had also pushed for Resident Evil 7 to have multiplayer and microtransactions during its conceptual phase.
"Right around that time, there was a big push at Capcom, a big 'marketing' push, saying 'we have to make the games players are asking for,'" franchise producer Jun Takeuchi said in 2022. "So we were being told 'make this, make that', it was really hard on the directors at the time. 'Online multiplayer' this, 'downloadable content' that. 'Ongoing service games! Microtransactions! Make a Resident Evil game that ticks all those boxes!'
“The idea of multiplayer got killed off pretty quickly. If we could properly put it together, we could make an exciting horror multiplayer game, but we didn’t really have any good ideas, so we set it aside. We went down the list, chopping them out, until we had marketing’s worst nightmare — a regular old single-player horror game."
Capcom is moving full speed ahead with many of its high-profile IPs, Resident Evil being one of them. The series just enjoyed a film adaptation directed by Zach Cregger, and a Code Veronica remake is set to release in February next year. Given that the devs of RE9 didn’t move forward with an online version of the game, it’s possible that we see another online Resident Evil title in the future — perhaps another Resident Evil Outbreak?

item.title: Jessica Chastain explained how she pulled off the terrifying facial expression she makes as the Other Mommy, saying that physical “pain” was a central part of getting her uncanny smile just right.
item.description:
Jessica Chastain explained how she pulled off the terrifying facial expression she makes in the Other Mommy, saying that physical “pain” was a central part of getting her uncanny smile just right.
Chastain stars in Universal Pictures’ Other Mommy, where she plays both the mother of a young girl and the entity that haunts her family. It’s a Coraline-style premise that adds another horror film to her steadily-growing roster of projects in the genre (IT Chapter 2, Mama, Crimson Peak).
The big draw for this film is Chastain’s horrifying transformation from a caring mother to a bloodthirsty entity wearing her skin. Trailers for the movie show the acclaimed actress in both roles; when she plays the entity, she wears a dead-eyed expression with a wide, almost painful-looking smile.
It turns out that this smile does, indeed, channel some element of physical pain, as told by Chastain during an appearance on Jimmy Kimmel Live where she explained how she came up with the entity’s distinct facial expression.
“I thought about this entity holding on the skin of a person, and maybe that’s the painful thing, like maybe you’re holding a box for a long time that’s very heavy. So the tension in your body, you have to hold this, and then, you have to smile, because you need a child to think you’re safe and approachable,” she said.
She then demonstrated the smile for the audience and even shed a tear right on cue. It was an impressive display of her acting ability, which Kimmel pointed out once her demo was done.
“I am a trained actress,” she joked. “You know what it is? I really felt the pain in my body, and that’s why, sometimes, you can see in the neck in the pictures — but then try to be as nice as possible. Don’t show your teeth.”
Thus far, early reviews for Other Mommy have been rather merciless; viewers who’ve seen it ahead of its October 9 theatrical release have called it “more silly than it is scary,” “truly dreadful,” and “masterfully cringe” on social media.
Viewers will have to judge for themselves when the film comes out tomorrow. For now, we can hope that Chastain’s impressive acting carries Other Mommy. That smile is certainly unsettling all on its own!

item.title: Forza Horizon 6 is finally coming to PS5 in January, and it will launch alongside a major expansion to the game.
item.description:
Forza Horizon 6 is finally coming to PS5 in January, and it will launch alongside a major expansion to the game.
A new trailer has confirmed that Forza Horizon 6 will race on to PS5 on January 26. It will arrive on the same day and date as the game's first major expansion, though no details have been revealed on what that will look like. As was the case with the Xbox and PC version of the game, players can pre-order the Premium Edition for extra goodies, including five days of early access to the game on PS5. Players who preorder any version of the game on PS5 will also get a pre-tuned Ferrari J50.
The news of the game's release date comes after rumors that Forza Horizon 6 would miss its initial 2026 release window for PS5. The news confirms that to be the case, but it will launch just in time to remove itself from GTA 6's blast radius. This should ensure it performs well on PS5 and give the game a healthy audience. Forza Horizon 5 was a massive hit on PS5 when it was released on the console last year, so there is a strong demand for its sequel.
IGN gave Forza Horizon 6 a 10/10 in its review, praising it for it dense map, technical achievements, and well-paced campaign.
"I’ll always concede Forza Horizon 3 may forever be my favourite open-world racer, because who doesn’t love driving around their own backyard, but make no mistake: Forza Horizon 6 is unequivocally the best," reads an excerpt from our review. "The new standard in open-world racing is here, and it’s a gundamn masterpiece."
